title: LTR depth distributions and estimated genome size
legend: The exact 380 primary LTR/Gypsy elements from 30 species are shown in the canonical phylogenetic row order. Gray horizontal outlines are log2-ratio densities with one pooled bandwidth, equal maximum widths, and tails trimmed to the observed range; violin widths do not represent sample size. Hollow points show all retained elements, jittered only vertically. Blue bars show released species medians of untransformed ratios; thin blue intervals are the released 95% intervals from 2,000 within-species element bootstraps. The right-hand labels give estimated genome size (pg/1C) and element count; n/a denotes unavailable genome size without imputation. The depth ratio is length-weighted mean per-base depth across both terminal LTRs divided by mean depth across the entire intervening sequence, including zero-depth bases. The primary branch retains LTR/Gypsy elements at least 3,000 bp long with at least five correctly parsed TEsorter domains, inclusive within-species 1.5-IQR fences, and at least 80% positive-depth coverage in all three regions. The dotted ratio-one line denotes equal mapped depth; it is not an empirically calibrated no-deletion baseline. This proxy is not an ectopic-recombination or DNA-loss rate. Elements are not independent biological replicates. Nineteen species with both genome-size estimates and primary LTR ratios contribute one median each (239 elements in total). The existing stored Pagel-lambda PGLS fit, coefficient interval, and predictions are reused without refitting: log10 median ratio is regressed on log10 estimated genome size. Stored genome coordinates and intervals in Gbp are divided by 0.978 to display pg/1C consistently with the other manuscript figures. This constant unit conversion leaves the log-log slope, its interval, P value, and all fitted ratio values unchanged. The slope is 0.024196 (95% t interval -0.560865 to 0.609257; P = 0.931489); lambda = 6.2e-09 at its lower boundary. The blue band is a coefficient interval for the fitted geometric mean, not an individual-species prediction interval. Gray bars show released genome-size intervals and element-bootstrap median intervals; these measurement uncertainties are not propagated through the regression. The interval permits associations in either direction; the nonsignificant test does not establish equivalence. Original source-tree branch lengths were retained in the stored fit; publication and calibration provenance remain unresolved. Genome sizes are IOD-derived estimates in pg/1C anchored to the D. fuscus assembly scale; they are not independently measured species C-values and their intervals exclude assembly-anchor uncertainty. This figure assembles existing results only; no filtering rules, data values, model estimates, or confidence intervals were changed. The excluded leave-one-species-out influence plot is not included.
alt_text: Thirty italic species labels align with gray horizontal density outlines, 380 hollow points, blue medians and intervals, a dotted equal-depth line, and genome-size/count labels at right. Nineteen labelled species medians with gray measurement intervals lie around a nearly horizontal blue PGLS line and a broad confidence band on logarithmic axes.
